uncited: The Cylinder Signed Distance Function computes the exact Euclidean distance from a query point to the surface of a finite cylinder defined by two endpoints and a radius.
It solves the problem of ray marching against capped cylindrical primitives, which are common in scene geometry and constructive solid geometry (CSG).
Unlike the infinite cylinder SDF, this method accounts for the end caps, returning the distance to the nearest point on the curved side, the top cap, or the bottom cap.

It is distinct from [Distance to Superquadrics](1561-distance-to-superquadrics.md) and [Torus Signed Distance Function](2864-torus-signed-distance-function.md) by its specific piecewise definition based on the projection onto the cylinder's axis.
- **Input**: A query point $v \in \mathbb{R}^3$, two endpoints $c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{R}^3$ defining the cylinder axis, and a radius $r \in \mathbb{R}^+$.
The method operates on standard 3D vectors and scalars.
The algorithm determines the closest point on the infinite line segment defined by $c_1$ and $c_2$, then computes the distance to that point, adjusting for the radius and the capped ends.
Let $h = \|dir\|$ be the height (length) of the cylinder.
*Note: If $h \approx 0$, the cylinder degenerates to a sphere or point; handle as a special case or return distance to $c_1$ minus $r$.*
Compute the parameter $t$ representing the normalized position of the projection of $v$ onto the line segment $[c_1, c_2]$.
Here, $t=0$ corresponds to $c_1$ and $t=1$ corresponds to $c_2$.
This is the closest point on the *infinite* line passing through $c_1$ and $c_2$.
Calculate the distance from the query point to the axis line, minus the radius.
This value is negative if the point is inside the infinite cylinder and positive if outside.
The final distance depends on whether the projection $p$ falls within the segment $[c_1, c_2]$ (i.e., $0 \le t \le 1$) or outside it.
-   **Case A: Inside the segment ($0 \le t \le 1$)**
The closest point on the capped cylinder is either on the side wall or on one of the end caps.

-   If $side\_dist < 0$ (inside the side wall), the point is inside the infinite cylinder.
The distance to the surface is the minimum of the distance to the side wall (magnitude of $side\_dist$) and the distance to the nearest end cap.
